1.explanation: The Java language definition (prism-java.js) contains the regular expressions that tokenize package and import statements. Its current pattern expects at least two segments (word.word) and hence doesn’t match a single identifier. Both prism-java.js and its minified counterpart need to be updated to allow one or more segments (e.g. changing the regex from something like /\w+(?:\.\w+)+/ to /\w+(?:\.\w+)*/).
1.bug_scenario: In the Java grammar, single‐segment package declarations and imports (e.g. “package baz;” or “import foo.Bar;”) aren’t being matched by the regex that highlights package names; only multi‐segment names with at least one dot (e.g. “baz.zap”) are picked up. As a result “baz” in “package baz;” and “foo” in “import foo.Bar;” aren’t highlighted correctly.

2.explanation: The files prism-java.js (and its minified counterpart) define Prism’s Java grammar rules—specifically the regex that captures package and import declarations under the “namespace” token. Because the pattern in these files doesn’t correctly match single-segment names, those declarations aren’t highlighted. Adjusting the regex in these two files will allow single-package names to be recognized and highlighted properly.
2.bug_scenario: When using Prism to highlight Java code, single-segment package and import declarations (e.g. “package baz;” or “import foo.Bar;”) are not being marked as namespaces, whereas multi-segment names (e.g. “package baz.zap;” or “import foo.bar.Bar;”) are. In other words, Prism’s Java grammar only highlights dotted package/import names correctly and fails on single-element names.
